assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology led from proglucagon-derived peptide biology to GLP-1 receptor agonists that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit now shown in large trials. Rare combination of basic physiological discovery and population-scale clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 secretion and physiology), Drucker (intestinotrophic and receptor biology, translation) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form and its synthesis) carry decisive roles. Knudsen's medicinal-chemistry work on long-acting analogues is important but more industrial; Habener-type contributions are not in the supplied credit and priority disputes exist.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation, multiple approved drugs and outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Disputed priority between the groups that identified the active GLP-1 peptide.
Whether the drug-development contribution (Knudsen) should be recognised alongside physiology, which would exceed three laureates.
My recollection of the discovery chronology is from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new therapeutic modality; originality in combining receptor engineering, costimulation and adoptive transfer is high.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (second-generation costimulatory CARs), June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR-T in leukemia) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy, TIL and early CAR work) form a plausible trio; Eshhar, Kuwana and others are not in the supplied credit, and credit among the many contributors is contested.
assessment.maturity: Approved products since 2017 with long-term follow-up; solid tumours remain largely unresolved but the haematological proof is mature.
uncertainties: Long-term safety (secondary malignancies, toxicity) and limited solid-tumour efficacy.
Credit for early chimeric receptor concepts outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery that ER stress is signalled to the nucleus through IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing and related branches established a new principle of intracellular signalling and proteostasis, relevant to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently defined the central pathway in yeast and mammals; a clean two-person prize is supported, with other UPR contributors (e.g. Ron, Harding) arguably secondary.
assessment.maturity: Foundational and heavily confirmed over 30 years; clinical translation is still emerging, but the basic science is mature.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is modest so far.
Boundary of credit relative to PERK and ATF6 branch discoverers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that blocking cell death, not only promoting proliferation, drives cancer, and led to BH3-mimetic drugs such as venetoclax with clinical benefit in CLL and AML.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led the Bcl-2 work on the translocation and the gene family; Vaux showed Bcl-2 prolongs survival and cooperates with myc. Strasser is a major later contributor. Others (Korsmeyer, Tsujimoto, Fesik/Souers on drug development) are not supplied, which complicates fair allocation.
assessment.maturity: Mature mechanistic confirmation and approved targeted drugs; timely.
uncertainties: Omission of deceased or non-listed key contributors such as Korsmeyer and Tsujimoto.
Apoptosis was already recognised in 2002, so novelty relative to that prize must be weighed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defined how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, linking infection, autoimmunity (e.g. interferonopathies), cancer immunity and ageing; a conceptually clean pathway with broad biological reach.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as the second messenger; Barber discovered STING. Their complementary roles support a two-person prize, though Ishikawa and others contributed to STING identification.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly confirmed and widely extended, but therapeutic agents are still in trials, so impact is partly prospective.
uncertainties: Credit for STING discovery shared with Ishikawa; possibly premature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: VLP-based HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical precancer, and population data now show large reductions in cervical cancer, a prevention achievement of global importance.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 virus-like particles; Frazer contributed key work on VLP/L2 expression and vaccine development; Zhou and others also contributed, and priority between the groups has been disputed.
assessment.maturity: Strong effectiveness evidence including cancer endpoints; the prize would be timely, though zur Hausen's 2008 prize covers the viral aetiology.
uncertainties: Priority dispute among groups (e.g. Zhou, Frazer, Lowy/Schiller).
Part of the field was previously honoured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib proved that selective inhibition of an oncogenic kinase can control a cancer, creating the template for targeted therapy and turning CML into a chronic disease.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery programme), Druker (clinical development and proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) is a plausible trio; Rowley and others earlier work on the Philadelphia chromosome, and Lasker 2009 already credited the core trio.
assessment.maturity: Exceptionally mature with decades of survival data; the long delay raises a question of whether other work now overshadows it.
uncertainties: Weigh Sawyers' resistance work against Zimmermann or other chemistry contributors, not in the supplied credit.
Whether the prize would be seen as a late recognition of a widely honoured achievement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Human genetics identified PCSK9 as a regulator of LDL receptor levels; loss-of-function variants lower LDL and cardiovascular risk, validating inhibitors that are now widely used. A strong example of genetics-led target discovery.
assessment.attribution: Abifadel/Boileau (gain-of-function families) , Seidah (biochemistry of PCSK9) and Hobbs/Cohen (loss-of-function variants and cardiovascular protection) all have decisive roles; five credited names exceed the maximum of three, so a trimmed trio is somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Antibody drugs approved and outcome trials positive, with siRNA and oral agents coming; reasonably mature.
uncertainties: Difficult allocation across five contributors with distinct decisive steps.
Lipid-lowering was already honoured by the 1985 statin-pathway prize; incremental novelty is debated.
